title: Amagi's Q2 profit jumps nearly 30-fold to Rs 74.8 crore as revenue hits a record Rs 475.8 crore
summary: Amagi reports Q2 profit jumps nearly 30-fold to Rs 74.8 crore
detailed: Bengaluru-based media SaaS company Amagi Media Labs reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 74.8 crore for the September quarter (Q2 FY27), nearly 30 times the Rs 2.5 crore it earned in the same quarter last year.
Its revenue from operations rose 27% year-on-year to a record Rs 475.8 crore, from Rs 374.8 crore.
Sequentially, net profit rose about 121% from Rs 33.9 crore in the June quarter, while revenue grew about 8.9% from Rs 436.9 crore.
That is already well above the Rs 71.7 crore profit Amagi reported for the whole of FY26, on revenue of Rs 1,505.6 crore.
sentences: Bengaluru-based media SaaS company Amagi Media Labs reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 74.8 crore for the September quarter (Q2 FY27), nearly 30 times the Rs 2.5 crore it earned in the same quarter last year.
Its revenue from operations rose 27% year-on-year to a record Rs 475.8 crore, from Rs 374.8 crore.

Amagi sells cloud software that lets TV networks and streaming companies launch, manage, distribute and earn advertising revenue from live, linear and on-demand content across cable, OTT and FAST (free ad-supported streaming TV) platforms, without owning traditional broadcast infrastructure.
Sequentially, net profit rose about 121% from Rs 33.9 crore in the June quarter, while revenue grew about 8.9% from Rs 436.9 crore.
Including other income, total income stood at Rs 501.9 crore, against Rs 389.6 crore a year ago and Rs 454.5 crore in Q1.
Total expenses rose about 9% year-on-year to Rs 419.3 crore from Rs 384.5 crore, well below the pace of revenue growth.
Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled, rising 114% to Rs 89.1 crore, and the margin widened 7.6 percentage points to 18.7%, the company said.
Net profit margin rose to 14.9% from 0.6% a year ago.
For the first half of FY27, revenue grew about 30% to Rs 912.7 crore and net profit reached Rs 108.7 crore.
That is already well above the Rs 71.7 crore profit Amagi reported for the whole of FY26, on revenue of Rs 1,505.6 crore.
Most of the gain came from costs growing slower than revenue.
In its shareholder letter, Amagi said its indirect operating expenses grew only 7% while revenue grew 27%.
R&D fell to 19.6% of revenue from 22.5%, sales, marketing and customer success to 21.7% from 24.5%, and general and administrative costs to 8% from 11.5%.
ESOP-related costs fell to Rs 25.4 crore from Rs 45 crore, partly because the year-ago quarter included a one-time catch-up of pre-IPO ESOP expenses.
The effective tax rate dropped to 9.4% from 50%, as the Indian business turned profitable and began setting off carried-forward losses.
Other income rose 76% to Rs 26.1 crore, mainly from returns on IPO money parked in fixed deposits and mutual funds.
The company cautioned that Q2 margins benefited from the timing of some planned senior hires, whose costs will now be incurred in later quarters.
It said the first-half adjusted EBITDA margin of 15.3% is “ a more representative near-term baseline ” for its profitability.
The September 2025 quarter included revenue from a large broadcaster migration, and Amagi said that excluding this, revenue would have grown 33%.
On a constant currency basis, reported growth was 15%.
Streaming Unification, Amagi's largest segment, grew 35% to Rs 261.1 crore and made up about 55% of revenue.
Monetization and Marketplace rose 28% to Rs 119.8 crore, while Cloud Modernization grew 9% to Rs 94.9 crore.
Channel deliveries on the platform rose 29% to 10,787, the number of distributors grew 24% to 477, and monetised ad impressions rose 65% to 16 billion.

During the quarter, Amagi launched four AI products: Amagi STUDIO for cloud-based live production, FANPULSE for turning live sports moments into social media content, Integrated Localization, and Agentic Network Operations.
Its news product NEWSPULSE is now live at local stations of a major US broadcast group, the company said.
“ Q2 marked new highs for revenue, Adjusted EBITDA and PAT.

Alongside stronger cash generation in the first half, this reflects the progress we have made in scaling the business with greater operating discipline, ” said Baskar Subramanian, co-founder, MD and CEO of Amagi.
Amagi ended September with Rs 1,774 crore in cash and treasury and no debt.
Adjusted operating cash flow was Rs 134 crore for the quarter.
The board appointed Bhaskar Ghosh, former chief strategy and innovation officer at Accenture, as an additional non-executive independent director for three years.
According to the filing , Ghosh has four decades of experience and is an independent director on the board of HDFC Life Insurance Company.
It also appointed co-founder and promoter Srividhya Srinivasan as whole-time director for five years, until 4 November 2031.
She keeps her role as CTO, with the designation “ Whole-time Director & Chief Technology Officer ” .
Srinivasan, who leads Amagi's new product and AI strategy, is the spouse of Subramanian, the filing said.
Both appointments need shareholder approval through a postal ballot.
The results also disclosed that on 22 October, Amagi was notified of a cyber extortion threat relating to one of its edge transmission sites.
The company said it informed CERT-In and does not expect the incident to have a material financial impact.
Founded in 2008 by Subramanian, Srinivasan and Arunachalam Srinivasan Karapattu, Amagi was valued at $1.4 billion in its last private funding valuation in November 2022.
Its investors include Accel, Norwest Venture Partners and Premji Invest, each of which partially offloaded their holdings through the IPO.
Its IPO raised Rs 1,788.6 crore at Rs 361 a share, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 816 crore and an offer for sale of about Rs 972.6 crore.
